full_judgment:
AFM Abdur Rahman J : By this Rule Nisi, dated 6-1-2008 the writ petitioner Md Habibur Rahman, challenged the legality and propriety of the judgment and order passed by the Administrator of Waqf on 6-9-2007 in connection with Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, having EC No. 8093, appointing the respondent No. 4 as mutwalli of the said Waqf Estate together with an advisory committee, rejecting the application for extension (renewal) of the period of the existing mutwalli committee, represented by the petitioner. 

 2. Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, having EC No. 8093, was created by Sheik Fakir Mahmud through a registered waqf deed being No. 810 dated 14-2-1940. As per the terms of the said waqf deed the sons and descendants of the waqif, who are pious and religious shall, by turn, be the mutwalli of the said waqf estate. The 3rd son of the waqif through the first wife, Hafez Moniruddin, was appointed as the first mutwalli of the said waqf estate. The waqf had two wives having each three sons. As per the terms of the deed after the death of the 1st mutwalli, Hafez Moniruddin, another descendent of the waqif named Tamizuddin was appointed as the second mutwalli of the waqf estate and after the demise of the second mutwalli, one Haji Ramizuddin Bhasani became the mutwalli. Meanwhile, one Abdul Maleq instituted Title Suit No. 178 of 1976, claiming title on the waqf property and the Administrator of Waqf, considering the circumstances, appointed a waqf, committee on 21-6-1995 for a term of two years under the presidentship of Haji Ramizuddin Bhasani and the other four persons from amongst the descendants of the waqif. The said mutwalli committee was extended for a further period of three years. But the legality of the said waqf committee was challenged by one Abdul Hossain before the Administrator of Waqf, who cancelled the said waqf committee by his order dated 17-11-1998 and appointed the said Abul Hossain as mutwalli of the waqf estate. This order of appointment of Abul Hossain as mutwalli was challenged by Haji Ramizuddin Bhasani in Writ Petition No. 3903 of 1998 and the Rule was made absolute through the judgment dated 24-5-1998 declaring the appointment of Abul Hossain as without lawful authority with further declaration that the waqf committee headed by Haji Ramizuddin Bhasani as lawful. The Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1292 of 1999 preferred by the Abul Hossain was dismissed on 6-3-2002. A further Review Petition No. 26 of 2002 was also dismissed. Later, the said Haji Ramizuddin Bhasani died on 16-1-2003 when the waqf committee was reconstituted with one of the descendents of the waqif Md Muslimuddin, son of Tamizuddin as chairman, who when died, the said committee was again reconstituted with the president ship of Haji Md Nabiullah. Thereafter, the tenure of the said committee was fixed for two years ending on 26-11-2006. Later, before the expiry of the tenure, the writ petitioner as the secretary of the said waqf committee, filed application before the Administrator of Waqf, respondent No. 2, praying for extension/renewal of the tenure of the waqf committee for five years and the same prayer was further renewed by another application filed on 21-1-2007. Thereafter, on 19-6-2005 one Nur Hossain, son of Abul Hossain, by filing application before the respondent No. 2, prayed for appointment as mutwalli of the said waqf estate and one Md Alamgir Siddique, the respondent No. 4, also filed application on 11-9-2006 praying for substitution of his name in place of Md Nur Hossain as the said Md Nur Hossain left for Italy. Thereafter, the Deputy Administrator of Waqf, respondent No. 3, took up the three sets of application for disposal and by the impugned order dated 6-9-2007 rejected the applications filed by the writ petitioner and allowed the application of Mr Md Alamgir Siddique, appointing him as mutwalli of the said waqf estate together with an advisory committee. By challenging the said judgment and order passed by the Deputy Administrator of Waqf-1, the petitioner obtained this Rule. 

 4. It has been asserted in the affidavit-in-opposition that this Rule is liable to be discharged since the petitioner after having preferred a suit against the self same impugned order, lost the same and preferred an appeal under section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 before the District Judge, Dhaka and having lost the same, preferred a revisional application before the High Court Division which was dismissed as not being pressed and therefore, the instant Rule is a misconceived one. It has been further asserted that the Administrator of Waqf upon considering the circumstances, of the waqf estate, came to a lawful finding that all the parties involved in the waqf estate, being beneficiary of the same, should be allowed to participate in the Administration of the waqf estate and, as such, the Administrator of waqf appointed the grand son of the first wife, the respondent No. 4, as the mutwalli and also constituted an advisory committee with the other beneficiary of the waqf estate and, as such, no illegality or irreasonability was committed by the Administrator of Waqf. 

 7. At the very outset of the hearing, while confronted with the query from this Court as to the maintainability of the instant writ petition in view of the impugned order passed under the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 which attracts appeal to the District Judge, the learned Senior Counsel, Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, admits that the instant appointment of the respondent No. 4, as mutwalli, is an appointment virtually under the Provision of section 43 and not under the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962, since, although the applications filed by one Mr Nur Hossain and substituted by the respondent No. '4 before the Administrator of Waqf on the allegation of committing irregularity and misappropriation of the waqf fund by the existing mutwalli committee, yet as the period of the mutwalli committee was expired and accordingly, the same was not in existence on the date of passing of the impugned order, the non-renewal of the period of earlier mutwalli committee cannot be treated as a removal of the mutwalli under the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962, rather the appointment of the respondent No. 4 as mutwalli must be treated as an appointment under the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962, since at that point of time there was no mutwalli or mutwalli committee existing in the said waqf estate. 

 8. The learned Senior Counsel, Mr Khondkar Mahbubuddin Ahmed, further admits that the petitioner preferred appeal against the impugned order before the District Judge, Dhaka as required under section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 and having lost there, the petitioner went to the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division, but his motion was ultimately rejected as being not pressed. Therefore, the learned Senior Counsel, Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, concedes to the legal aspect of the case that the instant writ petition is not maintainable. 

 9. But the learned Senior Counsel, Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, yet while taken this Court through the impugned order draws the attention of this Court to the illegality committed by the Administrator of Waqf in respect of appointing the respondent No. 4 for unlimited period and argues that the appointment of mutwalli under section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 must be for a limited period as it is the special power of the Waqf Administrator for appointment of mutwalli irrespective of the terms and condition, as embodied in the waqf deed. Therefore, the learned Senior Counsel contends that despite the non-maintainability of the instant writ petition, the merit of the case is in his favour, which the learned District Judge, Dhaka in the appeal, preferred by the writ petitioner, wrongly decided and rejected the same, taking the appointment of the respondent No. 4 as an appointment under the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962. The learned Senior Counsel prays for passing appropriate order by this Court. 

 10. On the other hand, the learned Advocate, Mr Golam Arshad, appearing on behalf of the Administrator of Waqf, while has taken this Court through the impugned judgment passed by the Waqf Administrator, strenuously argues, that the appointment of the respondent No. 4, as mutwalli of the Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, is an appointment under the Provision of section 43 the Waqf Ordinance 1962 and, as such, appeal lies against such order which the petitioner since filed before the District Judge, Dhaka and had lost the same, the petitioner preferred the revisional application before the High Court Division which was also rejected and, as such, this Rule on the self same cause is not sustainable and is liable to be discharged. 

 11. The learned Advocate, Mr Golam Arshad, further argues that the renewal of any tenure of mutwalli or mutwalli committee is in the absolute domain of the Administrator of Waqf, which cannot be claimed as a matter of right. Moreover the appointment of mutwalli under the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 cannot be said that it must be confined to a particular tenure, rather if it appears to the Administrator of waqf that no mutwalli was functioning in any waqf estate or appointment of mutwalli is barred by some reason or that the existing mutwalli became unsound in mind or could not function as mutwalli by any constraint the Administrator of Waqf can appoint any person as mutwalli of the said waqf estate and in that case the Administrator of Waqf is not bound to limit to tenure of the mutwalli. Therefore, the learned Advocate, Mr Golam Arshad argues, that no illegality was committed by the Administrator of Waqf through the impugned order. 

 15. While the mutwalli committee of Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, Bara Maghbazar, Dhaka headed by one Md Nabiullah with the present petitioner as secretary, was functioning from 29-11-2004 for two years, the writ petition filed application for renewal of the tenure of the said mutwalli committee on 12-10-2006 which was well within the period of tenure of the mutwalli committee. But when the impugned order dated 6-9-2007 was passed, the tenure of the said mutwalli committee was expired, meaning thereby that at the time of taking decision in respect of the office of mutwalli of Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, neither there was any mutwalli nor any mutwalli committee functioning in the said waqf estate. It appears that two other applications were filed before the Administrator of Waqf alleging certain allegations against the mutwalli committee, functioning of which was also taken up by the Administrator of Waqf along with the application filed by the writ petitioner on 12-10-2006 and renewed by further application dated 21-1-2007. The Administrator of Waqf after perusing all the applications and considering the circumstances of the said Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, appointed respondent No. 4 as the mutwalli of the said waqf estate to be assisted by an advisory committee of five persons. Therefore, it is crystal clear, that this action of the Waqf Administration is not an action regarding removal of a mutwalli or mutwalli committee of an waqf estate and appointment of a new mutwalli for the same under the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962, rather this is an appointment of mutwalli under the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962.  16. On the other hand, the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 involved a circumstance wherein an allegation against the mutwalli of a waqf estate was raised and upon such adjudication the mutwalli or the mutwalli committee is removed. The entire provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 is reproduced below; 

 17. Although the two other applications filed by the respondent No. 4 and one Nur Hossain raised allegations of misappropriation of fund and anomalies in the functioning of the mutwalli committee, yet while adjudication was made by the Administrator of Waqf on 6-9-2007 there was no mutwalli committee functioning or existing at that relevant point of time in the Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate. Therefore, under no chance the impugned order can be treated as passed under the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962, rather the same is an order passed under section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962. 

 18. Section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 provides for appeal before the District Judge. Since revision lies against the order of the District Judge under the Provision of section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, the petitioner correctly preferred the appeal before the District Judge, Dhaka, against the impugned order dated 6-9-2007 and then preferred a revisional application before the High Court Division against the dismissal of his appeal by the District Judge, Dhaka. But although the petitioner was liable to prefer civil petition for leave to appeal to the Appellate Division of the Bangladesh Supreme Court, instead he preferred the instant writ petition which is apparently erroneous. Therefore, this Court finds that this writ petition is not maintainable and accordingly, this Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 23. It appears that the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 is a Provision for filling the stopgap in a waqf estate wherein by some reason mutwalli can be appointed in a waqf estate and therefore any appointment made under the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 must be made for a limited period till the reason for stopgap is over. Therefore, the Administrator of Waqf while appointed the respondent No. 4 as a mutwalli of Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate ought to have fixed a period and since the period has not been fixed, the same can be fixed by the Administrator of Waqf after the disposal of this Rule, if the respondent No. 4 is otherwise competent to be the mutwalli of the waqf estate named Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, having EC No. 8093.
